title: Experiencias hasta ahora
description: Presente perfecto: experiencias de vida, resultados con already/yet/just, y cuándo usarlo frente al pasado simple.

grammarTopics.title: Presente perfecto: experiencias
grammarTopics.explanationEs: Se usa para experiencias de vida sin decir cuándo pasaron. Forma: have/has + participio pasado. 'I have been to Japan', 'She has never tried sushi'. Con ever en preguntas ('Have you ever...?') y never en negativas.

grammarTopics.title: Presente perfecto: already/yet/just
grammarTopics.explanationEs: Para acciones recientes con efecto en el presente. 'already' (ya, afirmativo): 'I have already eaten'. 'yet' (todavía/ya, en negativas y preguntas): 'Have you finished yet?', 'He hasn't called yet'. 'just' (recién): 'She has just arrived'.

grammarTopics.title: Presente perfecto vs pasado simple
grammarTopics.explanationEs: El pasado simple se usa con un momento definido ('yesterday', 'in 2010', 'last week'): 'I saw him yesterday'. El presente perfecto se usa sin momento definido o para experiencias: 'I have seen that film'. Si hay una fecha o palabra de tiempo pasado, va pasado simple.

teachingCards.bodyEs: El presente perfecto (have/has + participio) se usa para hablar de experiencias de vida, sin importar en qué momento pasaron.

examples.en: I have been to three different countries.
She has worked in two different companies.
examples.es: Ella trabajó en dos empresas distintas.

examples.en: I have traveled by train in Europe.
I have studied English for two years.
We have watched that series twice.

teachingCards.bodyEs: 'ever' (alguna vez) se usa en preguntas de experiencia; 'never' (nunca) en negativas. Ambos van entre el auxiliar y el participio.

examples.en: Have you ever lost your keys?
Has he ever managed a team?
I have never been to Asia.
She has never failed an exam.
Have you ever watched a horror movie alone?
examples.es: ¿Alguna vez miraste una película de terror solo?

payload.explanation: Presente perfecto: have + participio pasado. El participio de 'eat' es 'eaten': 'Have you ever eaten sushi?'
Con 'she' (3ª persona singular) el auxiliar es 'has': 'She has never been to Japan.'
Experiencia repetida sin fecha concreta → presente perfecto: 'I have seen' o 'I've seen'. Participio de 'see' = 'seen'.

segments: to London. It will be their first visit.
payload.explanation: El contexto ('first visit') pide el negativo con 'never', que va entre el auxiliar y el participio: 'They have never been to London.'
Pregunta de experiencia: Have + sujeto + ever + participio: 'Have you ever been to Paris?'

payload.prompt: He has ___ his homework, so he's free now.
payload.explanation: Participio pasado de 'do' = 'done': 'He has done his homework.'

acceptable: I have never been to France.
payload.explanation: Experiencia negativa de vida → presente perfecto con 'never': 'I have never been to France.'

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Have you ever tried Thai food?

options: Yes, I am trying it once.
payload.explanation: Respuesta sobre una experiencia → presente perfecto: 'I've tried it once.'

teachingCards.bodyEs: 'already' (ya) y 'just' (recién) van entre el auxiliar y el participio, en frases afirmativas sobre algo reciente.

examples.en: I have already had breakfast.
She has just sent the report.
We have already booked the hotel.
I have just finished my homework.
They have already watched the new episode.

teachingCards.bodyEs: 'yet' (todavía/ya) se usa en negativas y preguntas, siempre al final de la frase.

examples.en: I haven't had lunch yet.
Has she replied to the client yet?
We haven't booked the flights yet.
Have you finished the exercise yet?
They haven't watched the ending yet.

payload.prompt: I've ___ finished my homework. I can relax now.
payload.explanation: 'already' (ya) en afirmativas, entre el auxiliar y el participio: 'I've already finished.'
'yet' (ya/todavía) va al final de preguntas y negativas: 'Have you finished yet?'
'just' (recién) entre auxiliar y participio: 'She has just arrived.'
'already' va entre el auxiliar y el participio: 'I have already eaten lunch.'
En negativas se usa 'yet' al final: 'He hasn't called me yet.'
Verbo base → participio pasado. 'finish/arrive' son regulares (-ed); 'leave→left' y 'buy→bought' son irregulares.

acceptable: I have already finished my homework.
payload.explanation: 'ya' en afirmativa → 'already', entre auxiliar y participio: 'I have already finished my homework.'

payload.audioText: I have just finished cooking dinner. It's ready.

options: She has just finished cooking dinner.
She is going to cook dinner.

payload.explanation: El audio dice 'I have just finished cooking dinner' — acción recién terminada.

teachingCards.bodyEs: Si la frase incluye un momento definido del pasado (yesterday, last year, in 2010), usamos pasado simple, no presente perfecto.

examples.en: I met her last year.
She started this job in 2022.
We visited Rome two years ago.
I took that course last semester.
examples.es: Hice ese curso el semestre pasado.

examples.en: We watched that movie last weekend.
examples.es: Miramos esa película el fin de semana pasado.

teachingCards.bodyEs: Sin un momento definido, o para hablar de experiencia general, usamos presente perfecto.

examples.en: I have already met her.
She has worked in that role before.
examples.es: Ella ya trabajó en ese puesto antes.

examples.en: We have visited Rome before.
I have taken that course before.
We have watched that movie before.

payload.explanation: 'yesterday' es un momento definido del pasado → pasado simple: 'I met him yesterday.'
'last summer' marca un momento pasado concreto → pasado simple: 'She went to Italy last summer.'
Pregunta de experiencia sin fecha → presente perfecto: 'Have you ever been abroad?'
'in 2010' es una fecha concreta → pasado simple: 'We moved to this city in 2010.'
'When' pide un momento definido → pregunta en pasado simple con 'did': 'When did you see her?'

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Have you ever been to New York?

options: Yes, I have gone there in 2019.
payload.explanation: La pregunta es de experiencia, pero la respuesta da una fecha concreta ('in 2019') → pasado simple: 'I went there in 2019.'

acceptable: I went to the cinema yesterday.
I went to the movies yesterday.
I went to the movie theater yesterday.
payload.explanation: 'ayer' es un momento definido → pasado simple: 'I went to the cinema yesterday.' (no 'I have gone').
